decks.name: LeetCode #329 - Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
decks.description: Find the length of the longest increasing path in a matrix where you can move in four directions

cards.question: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix: Given an m x n integers matrix, return the length of the longest increasing path in matrix. From each cell, you can either move in four directions: left, right, up, or down. You may NOT move diagonally or move outside the boundary (i.e., wrap-around is not allowed).

solutions.name: Recursion
solutions.explanation: Use DFS from each cell to explore all possible increasing paths. For each cell, recursively try moving in all four directions if the next cell value is greater. Track longest path found. Base case returns 0 for out-of-bounds or non-increasing cells. Start DFS from every cell with prevVal=-inf. Explores all paths with exponential time complexity due to overlapping subproblems.

solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given matrix=[[9,9,4],[6,6,8],[2,1,1]]: Start dfs(0,0,-inf) with val=9. Try all four neighbors: dfs(1,0,9) finds 6<9 invalid, dfs(0,1,9) finds 9<=9 invalid, etc. From dfs(2,0,-inf) val=2: can go to (1,0)=6, then (0,0)=9, path length 3. Explores all paths from all cells, many redundant computations.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming (Top-Down)
solutions.explanation: Optimize recursion with memoization. Use dp dictionary to cache longest increasing path starting from each cell (r,c). Before computing, check if result exists in cache. DFS explores four directions from current cell, taking max path length. Start DFS from all cells, then return max of all cached values. Eliminates redundant computation by caching each cell's result.

solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given matrix=[[9,9,4],[6,6,8],[2,1,1]]: Call dfs from all cells. dfs(0,0,-1) with val=9 checks neighbors, finds no valid increasing paths, dp[(0,0)]=1. dfs(2,0,-1) with val=2: tries (1,0)=6>2, recurses dfs(1,0,2). dfs(1,0,2) tries (0,0)=9>6, recurses dfs(0,0,6)=1, so dp[(1,0)]=2, dp[(2,0)]=3. solutions.name: Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
solutions.explanation: Model matrix as directed acyclic graph where edges point from smaller to larger values. Compute indegree for each cell (count of smaller neighbors). Start BFS from cells with indegree 0 (local minimums). Process level by level, decreasing indegree of larger neighbors. Number of BFS levels equals longest increasing path. Iterative approach using topological sort to find longest path in DAG.
